summary: Himanshu Prabha Ray works in history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at Panjab University (~1966–1968), Cambridge (~1974–1975), and Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1980–1984), where she was Associate Professor (~1986–2006). She also held posts at LMU Munich, OCHS (2005), and the Humboldt Foundation (2014–2019).

Hiram W. Woodward works in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at Harvard College (~1958–1962) and Yale University (~1966–1975). He held positions at the University of Michigan (~1975–1982), the University of Vermont (~1982–1986), and the Walters Art Museum (~1986–2003).

Hirananda Sastri was an Indologist, historian, and archaeologist who studied at Dayanand Anglo-Vedic College, Oriental College, and Panjab University. He served at the Archaeological Survey of India (1903), held curatorial and archaeology posts in Jammu, Kashmir, and Baroda (1934–1942), and taught at DAV College.
Hiroaki Yokoyama is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed doctoral studies (博士後期課程) at Taisho University (attested 2013), where he has also held a post as a researcher (研究生).

Hirofumi Isoda is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at Tohoku University (~1963–1966). He served at Tohoku University as lecturer (~1969–1974) and associate professor (~1974–2002), and is attested as professor emeritus at Shimane University (1974).

Hirofumi Toda was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Seiren Matsunami (~1959–1965). He served as a professor at Tokushima University (~1980–2002) and held a post at Rissho University (attested 1985).
Hiroko Kawanami works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She studied under John Okell and Anna Allott, and served as a senior lecturer at Lancaster University (attested 2013–2016).
Hiroko Matsuoka works in Indology and philosophy. She was a doctoral student at Hiroshima University (attested 2006) and held a post at Leipzig University (attested 2016).

Hiromasa Tosaki works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied under Satkari Mookerjee, Shoren Ihara, Ryūshō Hikata, Seiren Matsunami, and Daniel H. H. Ingalls at Harvard, earning a PhD from Kyushu University (~1961–1966), where he was professor (~1979–1994).
Hiromi Habata specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. She received her Ph.D. from the University of Freiburg and held a researcher post at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~2006).
Hiromi Yoshimura works in Buddhist studies and Indology. Yoshimura held positions at Ryukoku University as a full-time lecturer (attested 1987) and later in 2006.
Hiromu Kitanishi was a Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology scholar. He studied at Otani University (~1946–1950) and later served there as professor (~1966–1991).
Hironori Tanaka is a scholar in Buddhist studies. Tanaka studied as a PhD student at Bukkyo University (attested 2015–2020) and also held an academic post there.

Hiroo Kashiwagi works in Buddhist studies. He completed doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo (~1958–1963) and held posts as professor at Matsusaka University (~1982–2000) and president of Matsusaka Women's Junior College (~1988–1996).
Hiroshi Aoyagi works in Japanology and related fields. He studied at International Christian University (~1977–1982) and held a post at Nanzan University (~2003).

Hiroshi Araki works in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from Kyoto University (~1983–2013) and held posts at Aichi Prefectural University (~1990–1994), Osaka University (~1994–2010), and the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (~2010).

Hiroshi Kanno works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1971–1982) and served as director at Soka University (~1987–2023) and the International Research Institute for Advanced Buddhology (~2002–2009).

Hiroshi Marui is an Indology and philosophy scholar educated at the University of Tokyo and Savitribai Phule Pune University, studying under Albrecht Wezler. He served at the Eastern Institute, Musashino University, and long-term as associate professor at the University of Tokyo.
Hiroshi Maruyama works in Indology and related fields. Maruyama held positions as a professor at Osaka University and head of Ayurveda Kenkyūkai (both attested 1987).
Hiroshi Nemoto works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. Nemoto earned an MA at Hiroshima University and later served as a professor there (attested 2015).
